title: Do you think any movie database (IMDB, Letterboxd, Mubi, etc.) is MOST accurate when it comes to suggesting similar films?

commenti.body:
It definitely depends on the popularity of the film because without humans providing necessary data for movies they’ve also watched, the alternative is individuals curating or algorithms finding matches based on genres. 

I think the third party system Letterboxd uses, Nanocrowd, is actually pretty good. But if the movie you’re looking at is somewhat obscure or rare what can they base the data on?

For me, that’s where I just look at the cast and crew. If you like a movie for a certain reason, click on the person responsible for that. See what else they’ve done. No guarantee you’ll like it as much, but it’s probably a decent indicator.

Yeah finding new movies based on directors, actors, etc. is what I've been doing recently.

I think IMDBs similar suggestions actually shine in the more obscure territory, I presume, because of the sheer number of users on that site and thus larger quantity of niche movie watchers. IMDB is both the best the best and worst movie site because of its scope. But yeah, because of its nature, its fair to say an algorithm will always point you towards the center of the bell curve rather than challenge you and push you deeper in cinema. A case for self-curation.

The recommendation system is the strongest selling point of criticker, have you checked that one? I used it for a bit but ended up using letterboxd instead because I have such a long list of films to watch anyway, and for me the main purpose of it is the library, to archive and display what I've seen, and letterboxd just has the best looking interface for that.
I haven't, thanks for the recommendation. Ah, I see there's a $5/mo charge to unlock all the recommendations..think I'll pass on that but what it shows looks pretty good.
I wasn't aware, not sure if it's a new addition or if I used the free version back then, it was many years ago.

The websites TasteDive and BestSimilar are both good for this kind of task. I was able to sometimes make some decent finds thanks to them. They combine "obvious" suggestions but also rare ones, based on the themes of the film or the director.
Thanks! Tastedive is great! It's getting me a lot more relevant recommendations that either Letterboxd or Mubi (I'm cross comparing). That will be my go to for now.

Your last sentence is the answer. I’m pretty new to getting more into film but with music I’ve rarely used “fans also like” stuff. It’s normally either super obvious or complete trash. So I’ve always found stuff from what the bands themselves recommend on social media, interviews, etc. Or what bands they’re touring with, what other bands are on the same label.

I’ve found so far the same is true for film. I’ve been either looking up lists/articles by people who’s opinion I value (Ebert, Sight & Sound) or just going through other stuff a director or actor worked on.

Sure, it takes a little more digging but honestly I’m already doing reading about a movie after I watch it anyway so it really doesn’t change much
>I prefer the hive mind of r/MovieSuggestions

check out [theyshootpictures.com](https://theyshootpictures.com) for finding directors similar to other directors

for instance [Jim Jarmusch](https://theyshootpictures.com/jarmuschjim.htm): Robert Bresson, John Cassavetes, Alex Cox, Hal Hartley, Werner Herzog, Aki Kaurismäki, Takeshi Kitano, Spike Lee, Yasujiro Ozu, John Sayles, Wayne Wang, Wim Wenders

MUBI is pretty great, as it is more playful and variated than the official Criterion Channel (IMHO).  I also appreciate the foreign film representation of Tubi, but you have to look for them knowing what you want in the first place.  And I go for a lot of Turner Classic Movies for my classic stuff, as that channel has not succumbed to Channel Drift, like Sundance or IFC.  Between those three channels I am good.   But in regards to your question, it really has to do with whether the algorithms really work on you or not.   There is a big difference between those for whowho
